body.statement:
Assume ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, ass:outer-ellipticity, ass:lift-regularity, ass:fixed-separated-grid, ass:kernel-symmetry, ass:kernel-mass, ass:kernel-order, ass:four-sample-design, ass:cell-ratios, and ass:polynomial-bandwidth.  Fix \(s\geq 8\) and
\[
 \frac{1}{2(s-2)}\leq a_h<\frac16.
\]
After \(a_h\) is fixed, choose \(\vartheta\in(0,1)\) so that \(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\), and define, for \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
 q_{k,n}(\vartheta)
 =\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{,2+2k+2\vartheta}}}
   +h_n^{,s-k-\vartheta}.
\]
Then there is a finite constant \(C_\star\), independent of \(P\) and \(n\), for which the program \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{crit}}\) gives the following conclusions uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).

First, if \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\) denotes the centered frozen-coefficient, affine-coordinate, frozen-pole part of the exact score \(\Psi_{g,h_n}\), then
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \left\|\Psi_{g,h_n}-\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\right\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C_\star,
\tag{1}
\]
and both the second elliptic response in \(\mathcal D_P\) and the complete scalar--harmonic response \(\mathcal H_P\) have cellwise \(L^2(P_g)\) norms bounded by \(C_\star\).  Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \frac{1}{L_n}
 \left\|
  \operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n})
  -\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n})
 \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
More explicitly, choose a coordinate ball \(U_j\) about \(y_j\), and a fixed smooth cutoff \(\chi_j\) supported in \(U_j\) and equal to one on a smaller ball.  At the pole \(y_j\) put
\[
 \Gamma_j(z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B(y_j)}}
 \log\left|B(y_j)^{-1/2}(z-y_j)\right|.
\tag{2a}
\]
Then the computable frozen-pole energy is
\[
 \frac1{L_n}\int_{\mathbb T^2}
 \{K_{h_n}^{\mathrm{per}}*(\chi_j\nabla\Gamma_j)\}(z)
 \{K_{h_n}^{\mathrm{per}}*(\chi_j\nabla\Gamma_j)\}(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{B(y_j)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y_j)}}.
\tag{2b}
\]
Thus the full transformed-KDE variable-coefficient response has the frozen-pole logarithmic covariance, with every generated-target within-cell cross term retained.

Second, for the opposite-fold plug-in scores,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G,\ r\in\{1,2\}}
 L_n^{-1/2}
 \left\|\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\right\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 >\epsilon\right}\longrightarrow0
\tag{3}
\]
for every \(\epsilon>0\).  This includes estimated-coefficient, moving-pole, and selected-lift errors; clipping and the measurable fallback occur with probability tending to zero uniformly.

Third, put \(u_n=(\widetilde f_g-f_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) and
\[
 R_{n,j}
 =\widetilde T_{P+u_n}(\widetilde y_j)
  -\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)-\mathcal D_P[u_n]_j.
\]
Then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}\max_{1\leq j\leq J}\|R_{n,j}|>\epsilon
 \right}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{4}
\]
and the deterministic order-minus-two bias satisfies
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{s-2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]
The bound behind (4) is the mixed two-endpoint estimate
\[
 \max_j|R_{n,j}|
 \leq C_\star\left(\max_g\|u_{n,g}\|_{C^{1,\vartheta}}\right)
          \left(\max_g\|u_{n,g}\|_{C^{0,\vartheta}}\right),
\tag{6}
\]
not a squared \(C^{1,\vartheta}\) bound.  The window above is maximal for these synchronized polynomial conditions: \(q_{2,n}(\vartheta)=o(1)\) and \(q_{0,n}(\vartheta)/h_n=o(1)\) are weaker, whereas
\(\sqrt{n/L_n}\,q_{1,n}(\vartheta)q_{0,n}(\vartheta)\to0\) is binding, and \(a_h=1/6\) is excluded.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(a_h<1/6\).  Since \(a_h>0\), the interval
\[
 0<\vartheta<\min\left\{1,\frac{a_h^{-1}-6}{4}\right\}
\tag{7}
\]
is nonempty; hence a fixed \(\vartheta\) satisfying \(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\) exists.  For later reference, the product of the two stochastic parts of \(q_{1,n}(\vartheta)\) and \(q_{0,n}(\vartheta)\), after critical normalization, is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{4+2\vartheta}}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2\vartheta}}}
 =a_h^{-1/2}(\log n)^{1/2}
   n^{-1/2+a_h(3+2\vartheta)}.
\tag{8}
\]
The exponent on \(n\) in (8) is negative precisely when
\(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\).  Lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility expands the other three nonnegative products and proves that, under \(s\geq8\) and the lower bound \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\), they vanish as well.  The same lemma gives
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{s-2}\to0,
 \qquad q_{2,n}(\vartheta)  o0,
 \qquad \frac{q_{0,n}(\vartheta)}{h_n}  o0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}q_{1,n}(\vartheta)q_{0,n}(\vartheta)  o0.
\tag{9}
\]
At \(a_h=1/6\), the right side of (8) equals
\(a_h^{-1/2}(\log n)^{1/2}n^{\vartheta/3}\) for every admissible \(\vartheta>0\), and even the formal endpoint \(\vartheta=0\) leaves the divergent factor \((\log n)^{1/2}\).  Thus the endpoint cannot be included.  Lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility also proves that the conditions involving \(q_{2,n}\) and \(q_{0,n}/h_n\) impose strictly weaker upper restrictions, establishing the asserted maximality.

We next invoke the analytic conclusion of lem:uniform-critical-estimates, whose hypotheses are exactly the maintained positivity, smoothness, ellipticity, lift-margin, separated-grid, kernel, sampling, and bandwidth conditions listed in the theorem.  That lemma constructs the periodic Green parametrix after pulling every kernel tangent to the original cell coordinate.  In its notation, the exact centered score admits
\[
 \Psi_{g,h_n}=\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}+E_{g,n},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \|E_{g,n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C,
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_g
 \|\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C\sqrt{L_n}.
\tag{11}
\]
Equation (10) includes the order-minus-two generated-target response and, by thm:nested-derivative, the complete inner and outer harmonic correction rather than setting either translation derivative to zero.  This proves (1) and the two stated componentwise \(L^2\) bounds.

For centered square-integrable random vectors \(X\) and \(E\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|\operatorname{Var}(X+E)-\operatorname{Var}(X)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq 2\|X\|_{L^2}\|E\|_{L^2}+\|E\|_{L^2}^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Apply (12) with \(X=\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\) and \(E=E_{g,n}\).  Equations (10)--(11) imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_g
 \frac{1}{L_n}
 \|\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n})
   -\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n})\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{L_n}}+\frac{C}{L_n}\to0,
\tag{13}
\]
because \(L_n=a_h\log n\to\infty\).  The frozen term in lem:uniform-critical-estimates is obtained by freezing only inside the energy parametrix.  To compute its covariance, write \(B_j=B(y_j)\).  Away from the pole, (2a) gives
\[
 \nabla\Gamma_j(z)
 =-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}
 \frac{B_j^{-1}(z-y_j)}{(z-y_j)^{\mathsf T}B_j^{-1}(z-y_j)}.
\tag{13a}
\]
With \(z-y_j=B_j^{1/2}r\omega\), \(\omega\in\mathbb S^1\), one has
\(dz=\sqrt{\det B_j}\,r\,dr\,d\omega\) and
\(\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}d\omega=\pi I_2\).  Hence, for fixed small \(r_0\),
\[
 \int_{h_n<|B_j^{-1/2}(z-y_j)|<r_0}
 \nabla\Gamma_j(z)\nabla\Gamma_j(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
 =\frac{B_j^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}L_n+O(1).
\tag{13b}
\]
Lem:uniform-critical-estimates proves uniformly that periodic mollification and the replacement of the elliptical annulus by a coordinate neighborhood change (13b) by \(o(L_n)\).  This proves (2b).  Consequently (13) proves (2), including the transformed-kernel and variable-coefficient replacement.  Since the four samples are independent by ass:four-sample-design, cross-cell covariances vanish; since each cell score is formed before its variance is taken, no within-cell generated-target cross product is discarded.

The opposite-fold part of lem:uniform-critical-estimates states, for every \(\epsilon>0\), exactly
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \max_{g,r}L_n^{-1/2}
 \|\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 >\epsilon\right}\to0.
\tag{14}
\]
Its proof uses \(q_{2,n}=o(1)\) for coefficient stability and
\(q_{0,n}/h_n=o(1)\) for the moving-pole Taylor bound.  It also shows that density clipping is inactive, normalization equals one, and ass:lift-regularity keeps both estimated maps on the selected population branch outside an event of uniformly vanishing probability.  Therefore (14) is precisely (3), including every error named there.

Finally, on the common good event supplied by lem:uniform-critical-estimates, the translation-aware two-endpoint expansion from thm:nested-derivative yields
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}|R_{n,j}|
 \leq C U_{1,n}(\vartheta)U_{0,n}(\vartheta),
 \qquad
 U_{k,n}(\vartheta)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \|u_{n,g}\|_{C^{k,\vartheta}}.
\tag{15}
\]
The moment and tail estimates in lem:uniform-critical-estimates give
\[
 U_{k,n}(\vartheta)=O_{\mathbb P}(q_{k,n}(\vartheta))
 \quad(k=0,1,2)
\tag{16}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\), and the complement of the good event has uniformly vanishing probability.  Combining (9), (15), and (16) gives, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}\max_j|R_{n,j}|>\epsilon\right}\to0,
\tag{17}
\]
which is (4).  The first limit in (9) is (5).  Equations (10), (13), (14), and (17) establish every item asked by the open-ended question, so the answer is affirmative on the maximal open polynomial bandwidth window.
body.justification: The theorem resolves the open question affirmatively by collecting the exact covariance replacement, plug-in score stability, and nonlinear remainder consequences of the uniform estimates.
body.gap: No residual transformed-KDE or moving-pole obligation remains under the maintained maximal bandwidth regime.
body.consumer: It discharges the analytic gate for the paper's complete inference and risk spine.
